solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reason a follower has not changed

blocks.note: the letter that follows A in the alphabet
'as is' describes something left unchanged

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a disciple has stayed exactly the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a follower' reads as a disciple, but in the alphabet B follows A; 'has not changed' is a two-word phrase meaning left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the grounds or underlying justification for something, a synonym for a reason.

clue.text: Help youngster to come out and challenge private

blocks.note: to beard someone is to confront them boldly
one's own is private, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Encouraging a young person to come out, then challenging a soldier of the lowest rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' suggests revealing one's sexuality and 'private' a soldier; the definition is really about a midwife urging a mother to push during childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: In labour a mother is told to push hard, which is what this phrase means, helping the baby be delivered.

clue.text: Song, right after a big chorus, for a cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and fall into a new order

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song where a big chorus is followed by a bird's call, as if scored for the cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only places R in the fodder; every letter of R plus 'a big chorus for a' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional English folk ballad, made famous by Simon and Garfunkel, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Finding this gemstone requires patience

blocks.note: first meaning: a single diamond or gem set on its own
second meaning: the one-player card game, called patience in Britain

explanation.surface: Hunting for a particular jewel takes a lot of patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patience' reads as the virtue, but it is the British name for the one-player card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a single jewel set alone in a ring and the card game Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Being sluggish, a pet dog rolls back over

indicators.note: rolling back turns the word round so it reads from end to start
to be over something is to cover it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a strop

explanation.surface: A lazy pet dog rolls over onto its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like the dog itself but is a sulk (STROP, informal British); 'Being sluggish' is a noun phrase, a being that is slug-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs and snails belong to this class of molluscs, so a sluggish creature in the literal sense is one.

clue.text: Good mimic makes you yawn

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: A skilled impressionist is so tedious they make you yawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good mimic' reads as praise for an impressionist, but it splits into a one-letter abbreviation and a verb for copying.
explanation.definitionFit: To open the mouth wide, as in a long stare or a sleepy breath, is a close synonym.

clue.text: Web areas advance, given the same power supply?

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
do is short for ditto, the same
the mains is the household electricity supply

explanation.surface: Asking whether parts of the internet move ahead when they share one electricity source.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB for an advance on pay is British informal usage, as is DO for ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: Websites are organised into named sections under a parent domain, which are internet regions.

clue.text: Flew as fighter pilot, in a way

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, enclosed on both sides

blocks.note: an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone flew as a fighter pilot, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flew' suggests aircraft, but it means moved fast; 'in a way' sounds like 'sort of' but is a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew in the sense of rushed or hurried along at speed is a common synonym.

clue.text: For a new salon, creates things

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: per means for each, for a, as in 'per day'
taken as written
to effect a change is to create it

explanation.surface: A business owner sets up a fresh hairdressing salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a' looks like ordinary connecting words but is PER; 'things' is the definition, tucked at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: One's things, in the sense of belongings, are the private possessions a person carries or owns.

clue.text: March in Paris, from out of Paris

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
signals that the next word is to be put into French
de is the French for from

explanation.surface: A protest march in Paris, coming from outside the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of Paris' looks like 'away from Paris' but means 'out' as Parisians say it: the word is French and English borrows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Démodé is French for unfashionable, out of date, so it is how Paris says something is out.

clue.text: Fast 14

indicators.note: the cross-referenced entry opens with a word meaning operating or in motion, so the letters that follow are put to work in a new order

blocks.note: 14-across is WORKING CAPITAL; its second word is the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: Write out 14-across in place of the number: 'Fast working capital' then reads as a definition, an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at a clip means going at a brisk pace, an idiom for quickly or speedily.

clue.text: Deer and sheep bound for cover

blocks.note: a buck is a male deer
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Deer and sheep leap away to hide in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests leaping animals, but it hints at bookbinding, where the answer is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is stiffened cloth traditionally used to cover books and line garments, so it is a covering material.

clue.text: Argument has girl coming out worried

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman making her society debut, 'coming out'
something that worried you ate at you

explanation.surface: A family row breaks out because a daughter making her debut is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is in the 'eating at' sense, past tense, giving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument between opposing sides, as in a parliamentary discussion, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Race track’s skilled driver

blocks.note: good at something means skilled
a driver is a golf club of the kind called a wood

explanation.surface: A racing circuit is home to a talented motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a racing driver, but it is the golf club; Goodwood is a racecourse and motor circuit in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwood is a famous English venue for horse racing and motor racing, so it is an example of a race track.

clue.text: Sugar etc extremely good for cooking dessert

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of the word
cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe note: sugar and other ingredients are just right for making a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar etc' looks like a list of ingredients and is, but only as letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked custard made with eggs and milk is a classic sweet course, so it is an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Means to trade on A1?

blocks.note: a machine that is on is in operation
A1 and capital both mean first-rate, excellent

explanation.surface: Asks whether a business could trade along the A1, Britain's longest road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, but here it is the old British exclamation of approval, as is capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Working capital is the money a business has available for day-to-day operations, its means of trading.

clue.text: I point and shout “Rover!”

blocks.note: taken as written
a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler
to rant is to shout angrily

explanation.surface: Someone points and calls out a dog's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' in quotation marks looks like a dog's name being called; it is a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer with no fixed home, and an itinerant is a person who travels from place to place.

clue.text: Mean to cross river with a fish

indicators.note: crossing something means spanning it, so one piece stretches across and around the other

blocks.note: stingy means mean with money
R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone plans to ford a river while carrying a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, 'intend to', but it is the adjective for tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature with a venomous tail spine, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Ancient land, extremely dry?

blocks.note: super- means to an extreme degree, as in superfine
dry means abstaining from drink, and continent means exercising self-restraint

explanation.surface: Asks whether an ancient country was a very arid place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' suggests a desert, but it is the teetotal sense, matched by continent meaning self-restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Pangaea was a vast landmass of the distant geological past, and that is what this term names.

clue.text: City had not been prepared for rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: had been, in short, was
something not cooked or prepared is raw

explanation.surface: A city was caught unready for an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Warsaw Uprising of 1944, but 'rising' is the instruction for a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, so it is an example of a major European urban centre.

clue.text: Saw a head of state outside house, having gentleman around

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
being outside something means surrounding it on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written
PM, the Prime Minister, taken as the leader of the country
HO is the abbreviation for house
sir is the title of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a leader outside a home, with a gentleman nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying, and an aphorism is a short pithy statement of a truth.

clue.text: “P” breaks for cool beast

indicators.note: breaking apart to make room for something lets it sit in the gap

blocks.note: the Greek letter rho is written P
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A letter P gives way to make room for a trendy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted P looks like an English letter; it is the capital form of the Greek rho.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is a large horned mammal, so it is an example of a beast.

clue.text: Loud noise, ultimately in head, may do so

definitions.text: Loud noise, ultimately in head, may do so

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept
placing one thing in another puts it inside, enclosed

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
the last letter of the word
a dean is the head of a college or faculty
surface padding completing the whole-clue definition

explanation.surface: A loud noise inside your head may well damage your hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: 'head' reads as the body part, but in the wordplay it is a college head.
explanation.definitionFit: A very loud sound can cause temporary hearing loss, and the clue as a whole describes that effect.

clue.text: Surgery reminder in Christmas card

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: A note from the doctor's surgery slipped into a Christmas card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgery' suggests a British doctor's office sending a reminder; it is an operation, leaving a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation leaves a healed mark on the skin, a lasting physical memento of the procedure.

clue.text: I am playing with ants’ legs

indicators.note: playing with something means fiddling with it, so the letters get moved about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A child admits to toying with the legs of ants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legs' reads as insect limbs but is the sporting sense, as when a long-running show 'has legs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having legs means having staying power to keep going, which is endurance.

clue.text: Unscrupulous type in court. No conclusion reached

indicators.note: with no conclusion reached, the ending never arrives, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court

explanation.surface: A dodgy character stands trial, but the case ends without a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is a division of the High Court in England; lose its last letter. Chancer is British slang for an opportunist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is British slang for an opportunist who takes risks and bends rules for personal gain.

clue.text: Syntax concern in instruction book

blocks.note: the Word, the Bible, is the book
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: A point of grammar dealt with in a manual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instruction book' reads as a manual, but the two pieces must be swapped round, a joke on the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax governs how words are arranged in a sentence, so the sequence of words is its central concern.

clue.text: Smoking? You shouldn’t have a pen

blocks.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is 'you shouldn't have'
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A smoker is told off for carrying a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking' suggests cigarettes; it is slang for attractive, as in 'smoking hot'. TA is British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British slang for sexually attractive or appealing.
